queries.rationale: Searches for repositories that maintainers tagged with the "microfrontend" topic. The topic is an explicit declaration that the project concerns micro-frontends and serves as a signal for selecting candidates (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 1). Each spelling is queried separately because GitHub treats differently spelled topics as distinct labels.

Searches for repositories that maintainers tagged with the "microfrontends" topic. The topic is an explicit declaration that the project concerns micro-frontends and serves as a signal for selecting candidates (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 1). Each spelling is queried separately because GitHub treats differently spelled topics as distinct labels.

Searches for repositories that maintainers tagged with the "micro-frontend" topic. The topic is an explicit declaration that the project concerns micro-frontends and serves as a signal for selecting candidates (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 1). Each spelling is queried separately because GitHub treats differently spelled topics as distinct labels.

Searches for repositories that maintainers tagged with the "micro-frontends" topic. The topic is an explicit declaration that the project concerns micro-frontends and serves as a signal for selecting candidates (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 1). Each spelling is queried separately because GitHub treats differently spelled topics as distinct labels.

Searches for repositories that mention "microfrontend" in their name, description or README. The mention is a signal for selecting candidates and does not confirm that the project implements micro-frontends. The query is partitioned by creation month, starting in 2019, so that each slice stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 1).

Searches for repositories that mention "microfrontends" in their name, description or README. The mention is a signal for selecting candidates and does not confirm that the project implements micro-frontends. The query is partitioned by creation month, starting in 2019, so that each slice stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 1).

Searches for repositories that mention "micro frontend" in their name, description or README. In GitHub search, this expression is equivalent to "micro-frontend", so a single query covers both spellings. The mention is a signal for selecting candidates and does not confirm that the project implements micro-frontends. The query is partitioned by creation month, starting in 2019, so that each slice stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 1).

Searches for repositories that mention "micro frontends" in their name, description or README. In GitHub search, this expression is equivalent to "micro-frontends", so a single query covers both spellings. The mention is a signal for selecting candidates and does not confirm that the project implements micro-frontends. The query is partitioned by creation month, starting in 2019, so that each slice stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 1).

Searches for repositories that maintainers tagged with the "module-federation" topic. The topic indicates the use of a composition technology, even when the project does not use the term micro-frontend (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 2).

Searches for repositories that maintainers tagged with the "single-spa" topic. The topic indicates the use of a composition technology, even when the project does not use the term micro-frontend (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 2).

Searches for repositories that mention "module federation" in their name, description or README. The signal is the mention of the technology, independently of the term micro-frontend. The query is partitioned by creation month, starting in 2019, so that each slice stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 2).

Searches for repositories that mention "single-spa" in their name, description or README. The signal is the mention of the technology. Quotation marks prevent the search from splitting the term at the hyphen. The query is partitioned by creation quarter, starting in 2019, so that each slice stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 2).

Searches for READMEs that mention "web components" together with "micro frontends". Web Components is a native browser API and leaves no artifact that, on its own, indicates application composition. The query therefore requires the term to appear together with micro-frontends, which excludes component libraries.

Searches for READMEs that mention "web components" together with "microfrontends", without a space. This is the previous query's variant for the other spelling, because the search treats "microfrontends" and "micro frontends" as distinct terms.

Searches for package.json files declaring dependencies in the "@module-federation" scope. A declared Module Federation dependency is a technology signal, regardless of the use of the term micro-frontend (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 2). The query is partitioned by file-size ranges so that each range stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query.

Searches for package.json files declaring the "@originjs/vite-plugin-federation" package, the module federation plugin for Vite. This dependency indicates Module Federation in Vite projects (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 2). The query is partitioned by file-size ranges so that each range stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query.

Searches for package.json files declaring the "@angular-architects/module-federation" package, the Module Federation integration for Angular. This dependency indicates Module Federation in Angular projects (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 2). The query is partitioned by file-size ranges so that each range stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query.

Searches for package.json files declaring the "@angular-architects/native-federation" package. Native Federation is an additional composition approach allowed by the protocol, and the declared dependency is the signal sought.

Searches for package.json files mentioning "single-spa". A declared single-spa dependency is a technology signal (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 2). The query is partitioned by file-size ranges so that each range stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query.

Searches for JavaScript files containing "ModuleFederationPlugin" and "remotes". A configuration declaring remotes is evidence of composition, not merely of a dependency's presence. The query is partitioned by file-size ranges so that each range stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query.

Searches for TypeScript files containing "ModuleFederationPlugin" and "remotes". This is the same query used for JavaScript configurations, applied to TypeScript files. The query is partitioned by file-size ranges so that each range stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query.

Searches for code files containing "registerApplication" and "singleSpa". Application registration in single-spa is evidence of composition. The query is partitioned by file-size ranges so that each range stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query.

Searches for code files containing "customElements.define" and "registerApplication". The signal sought is custom elements registered as applications, which may indicate a combination of Web Components and single-spa.

Searches for repositories that mention "frontend composition" in their name, description or README. This is a broader term than micro-frontend, included to expand discovery coverage (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 3).

Searches for repositories that mention "frontend decomposition" in their name, description or README. This is a broader term than micro-frontend, included to expand discovery coverage (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 3).

Searches for repositories that mention "frontend orchestration" in their name, description or README. This is a broader term than micro-frontend, included to expand discovery coverage (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 3). The query is partitioned by creation quarter, starting in 2019, so that each slice stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query.

Searches for repositories that mention "federated modules" in their name, description or README. This is a broader term than Module Federation, included to expand discovery coverage (protocol, section 3.1, procedure 3).

Searches for repositories that mention "micro apps" and "frontend" in their name, description or README. Frontend micro-applications are a term associated with micro-frontends, cited in protocol section 3.4.7. The query is partitioned by creation quarter, starting in 2019, so that each slice stays below the GitHub search limit of 1,000 results per query.
